text:
Mia (Sales): Heads up — Acme Health POC needs Private/VPC setup. They want PrivateLink + hosted API key scoped to the POC and a Dedicated pool for heavy load tests. Can infra confirm subnet/route requirements and a short handoff checklist?
John (Solutions): Yep. Need: interface endpoint (com.amazonaws.vpce...), 2 x private subnets in different AZs, route table entries to the ENIs, security group allowing outbound 443 to our endpoint. Also we need a short-lived API key for the POC.
Lee (Infra): For PrivateLink, we'll publish a service name once we create the endpoint service. Customer then creates an interface VPC endpoint in their acct and accepts. Requirements: private DNS enabled (optional but makes curl hostnames work), SG inbound from their subnets on 443, and no NAT required for egress to our endpoint.
Carla (SRE): Note on routing: don't put the endpoint ENIs in a public route table. Example route table snippet for their AZ subnets:
```
RouteTable:  rtb-xxxx
Destination: 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-xxxx  (for general egress)
Destination: 10.85.0.0/24 -> local (local VPC)
# PrivateLink is interface endpoints (ENIs) attached to subnets — no special route to add for interface endpoints
```
Also if they use TGW, they must attach the VPC endpoint to the same VPC or use proxying; cross-VPC through TGW to interface endpoints isn't supported by default.
Devon (NetOps): For the Dedicated pool access: we'll add an allowlist tag + customer org ID so their traffic is routed to the reserved capacity. Need their AWS account ID and test CIDR ranges. We'll also need their contact for cross-account acceptance.
Mia (Sales): I have account ID 123456789012 and Acme's network contact is emily@acmehealth.com. They asked about sample security group rules and a curl test.
John (Solutions): Sample SG (customer side) inbound:
```
Type: HTTPS
Protocol: TCP
Port: 443
Source: 10.85.0.0/24  # their app subnets
```
On our side SG to allow responses: allow ephemeral high ports from our ENIs. For curl test: after endpoint exists run `curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health` (private DNS) or `curl -v https://vpce-<id>.execute-api.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/v1/health` if they prefer the VPCE-specific hostname.
Carla (SRE): Security note — if they enable private DNS we recommend they don't override our CNAME in Route53. For strict environments we can provide a dedicated host name and TLS cert pinned to that. Also confirm KMS access if they want us to call KMS in their account (we do not assume KMS access by default).
Devon (NetOps): Acceptance flow: 1) we create service -> give service name 2) they create VPC endpoint and send acceptance 3) we accept 4) they validate DNS + SG. Share screenshots of endpoint state. We can also provide a CloudFormation snippet to speed creation.
Mia (Sales): Can we get a quick CloudFormation snippet for them? Also need a POC API key TTL of 7 days.
Lee (Infra): I'll put together a minimal CFN for interface endpoint + SG and attach to ticket. For API key: we can issue a scoped key limited to the POC project and tag it. We'll rotate after 7 days automatically.
deploy-bot: Ticket INFR-3221 created for Dedicated pool reservation (ETA 72h) and PVCE service creation.
John (Solutions): CFN snippet (minimal):
```
Resources:
  VPCEndpointSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: "Allow app -> PrivateLink"
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 443
          ToPort: 443
          CidrIp: 10.85.0.0/24
  InterfaceEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Properties:
      ServiceName: !Ref ServiceName
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
      VpcEndpointType: Interface
      SubnetIds: !Ref PrivateSubnetIds
      SecurityGroupIds:
        - !Ref VPCEndpointSecurityGroup
```
Carla (SRE): We'll also need a quick smoke test plan for Acme: 1) create endpoint 2) verify ENIs in subnets 3) private DNS resolves to interface endpoints 4) `curl /v1/health` 5) run a small load to route through Dedicated pool.
Mia (Sales): Perfect. Can infra schedule the acceptance step tomorrow morning? Customer prefers a Friday window for the initial handoff.
Lee (Infra): We can do Friday 09:00 PT. I'll allocate a brief maintenance window and send the service name to you by EOD.
Mia (Sales): Thanks — I'll confirm with Acme and send contact details to INFR-3221. :thumbsup:
Carla (SRE): One last thing — if they insist on VPC peering instead of PrivateLink, we need to discuss cross-account route table propagation and NAT considerations. PrivateLink is simpler for our infra and keeps traffic to interface endpoints.
Mia (Sales): Ack. I'll push PrivateLink as recommended.
John (Solutions): I'll attach the CFN and the curl test commands to the ticket.
deploy-bot: Comment added to INFR-3221: "Requested service name and API key TTL: 7d"
Mia (Sales): Closing loop here once Friday is scheduled. Thanks team!
